alana: Heads up, weird TS DX hit: our published SDK's overloads collapse to `any` in edge ESM consumers (Cloudflare worker). Node imports fine.

ben: Can you paste the public declarations and package fields? usually exports/types mismatch.

alana: Minimal export:```ts
export function send<T>(req: { body: T }): Promise<Res<T>>;
export function send(req: { body: unknown }): Promise<Res<any>>;
```
In an edge app `sdk.send({ body: { x: 1 } })` shows body: any.

sahil: Are you shipping different .d.ts for cjs/esm and relying on `types` to pick the right one? bundlers + edge toolchains sometimes ignore package.exports types keys.

alana: package.json has module/main/types and exports with import/require, but types points at dist/cjs/index.d.ts. We built types via rollup-dts on publish.

ben: rollup-dts reorder overloads sometimes. I recommend `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` and point types to that output. Also add `exports.import.types` mapping.

sahil: Alternatively, prefer a single generic signature to avoid ambiguous overload resolution: `export function send<T = unknown>(req: { body: T & {} }): Promise<Res<T>>;` tends to be more stable across resolvers.

alana: Interesting. Would adding root index.d.ts that re-exports stable surface help IDEs?

ben: Yes, a tiny root d.ts that re-exports the right symbols reduces surprises for editors while exports map handles runtime.

edge-bot: deploy-check: detected package with both cjs/esm types; recommend explicit types in exports.

sahil: Also add a consumer CI job: install the built package into a minimal worker repo and run tsc with module=esnext and moduleResolution=node16. That catches this early.

alana: Action: switch to tsc declarations, add exports.types mappings, add consumer CI test, and try single-generic refactor. I'll open PR and attach repro.

ben: If you want, I can help craft the typesVersions map for backwards TS compatibility.

alana: Thanks — assigning to @ben and @sahil. Will post repro link soon :sparkles:
